> An NHS trust in Walsall says an AI scribe cut its clinicians' note-writing to under four minutes a patient.
>
> The tool is called Heidi. It listens to the consultation on a phone and writes the clinical notes, and a clinician reviews them, edits where needed and approves them before anything goes on the record. One emergency consultant, Dr Jamil Aslam, says it saves him six minutes a consultation, and after an eight-month pilot it's being rolled out across two trusts.
>
> There's one thing it hasn't shown. In July the BBC reported the tool was improving NHS waiting times, then changed its headline, because evidence for that has not yet been published.
>
> The typing time was measured. The waiting times haven't been shown.
>
> So when you try AI, pick the one job you'll time before and after, and only claim what those numbers show.
>
> Follow for one real AI story a day, and what it means for your business.
